rationale: Select the directional nearest nonzero colours. In demonstration 1, the zero at (0,2) has nearest colours (absent,3,absent,2) in up/down/left/right order and becomes 2. In demonstration 5, (4,1) has (3,absent,absent,1) and becomes 9. Other observed directional keys preserve their colours.

Select own colour and zero-based coordinates modulo 3. Zeros become 3 at residues (0,2), (2,1), and (2,2), and become 8 at (1,1); other colours and residues stay unchanged. Demonstration 1 shows these changes at (0,2), (2,1), (2,2), and (1,1), while demonstration 7 repeats them across larger coordinates.
